questions.question: What is the speed limit on streets and highways if no sign is posted?

options.text: 70 mph
55 mph
45 mph
30 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph
questions.explanation: The default speed limit is 55 mph. Always follow posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road is blocked ahead.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely. After stopping, proceed only when the way is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn at this location.

questions.question: What is most important when driving through curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit the whole time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's weight may pull it to the side, so reduced speed helps you stay in control.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an accident scene?

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help is not there yet.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Only stop if you are involved in the accident or if emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving past the scene. Do not stop just to look.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming at the next intersection.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs?

options.text: Posted everywhere there is a present danger.
Signs that tell you what you must or must not do.
Diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
Signs that warn about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs that tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black lettering on white. They show speed limits, passing rules, and other driving requirements.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be prepared to stop if traffic requires it. You must stop if there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: It can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
It has a triangular shape.
It is blue with black lettering.
A suggested speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A suggested speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Speed signs on curves and turns show a recommended safe speed. You may drive faster in good weather, but always drive slower in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a sharp curve in the direction of the arrow. In this case, it points left. You may see several of these signs throughout a curve.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers account for?

options.text: Large vehicles need more distance to stop.
Large vehicles need less distance to stop.
Large vehicles are quieter.
Large vehicles drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large vehicles need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you. Do not block the truck driver's view of the road.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Wait until you are on the exit ramp to slow down. Do not slow down before you enter it.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist does not obey traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists do not have to obey traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They will always get a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws as drivers. Both bicyclists and drivers who break traffic laws can be ticketed.

questions.question: You are in an intersection waiting to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to ask drivers to let you through.
Drive around the rear of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane early. Slow down only after you are fully on the exit lane.

questions.question: An oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk your horn to get attention. If the other driver does not move, steer to the right. Do not steer left because they might correct at the last second and you will still crash. Brake hard and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: You are in a line of traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can completely cross the tracks without stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can completely cross the tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before entering the tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely without stopping. Never pass other vehicles at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any railroad tracks.

questions.question: What is a work zone?

options.text: It can be moving or staying in one place.
It is marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be moving or staying in one place.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be in one place or moving. Moving work zones include vehicles that stripe lines, mow, or remove snow. Work zones use orange signs with black letters or symbols. Slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the side with the broken line.
You can pass from the side with the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, you can pass from the lane with the broken line.

questions.question: To get ready for what is ahead on the road, you should:

options.text: Look at the whole road and both sides continuously.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Look at the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the whole road and both sides continuously.
questions.explanation: Your ability to handle dangerous situations depends on spotting problems before you reach them. Looking far ahead does not mean staring at the center of the road. You need to look at the entire road, including both sides.

questions.question: When using a roundabout or rotary island, drivers should:

options.text: Yield to traffic entering the roundabout.
Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Drive in a clockwise direction.
Stop inside the rotary island.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection that flows counterclockwise around a central island with no traffic signal. You must enter from the right, give way to traffic already in the roundabout, and follow the circle to the right until you reach your exit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a merge ahead. Two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are about to become one lane.

questions.question: You may drive in HOV lanes if:

options.text: You are driving faster than other traffic.
You are driving slower than other traffic.
Your vehicle has two or more people in it.
You are trying to get somewhere quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle has two or more people in it.
questions.explanation: Some highways reserve the left lane for vehicles with two or more people or hybrid/low-emission vehicles. These High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes are marked by signs and diamond symbols on the road. They are separated from other lanes by a striped buffer zone. You can only enter and exit HOV lanes at marked points.

questions.question: When you double a car's speed, you increase the force of impact by:

options.text: Two times.
Three times.
Four times.
Nothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four times.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the greater the impact force of your vehicle. When you double the speed of a car, the force of impact increases by four times.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time:

options.text: The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A dashed line means drivers next to the line can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal driving speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Go faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You may turn right or left at a steady green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must give way to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: If you are convicted of driving under the influence for the first time, you may face:

options.text: Only a fine.
A fine and community service.
A fine, community service, and jail time.
A fine, community service, jail time, DUI school, license revocation, and an Ignition Interlock Device.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fine, community service, jail time, DUI school, license revocation, and an Ignition Interlock Device.
questions.explanation: Penalties for a first DUI conviction may include a fine, community service, jail time, license revocation, and an Ignition Interlock Device. Penalties increase for each additional DUI conviction.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A solid yellow arrow:

options.text: Is never used as a traffic signal.
Means the same as a circular yellow traffic light.
Means you can turn in the direction the arrow points.
Means a green arrow is coming next.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means the same as a circular yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a yellow traffic light. When you see a solid yellow arrow, slow down and get ready for a red light.
